{
  "thinking": "Empty table and a 10-minute clock, so the picture has to be simple and easy to read from its outline. I'll take the pad and sketch a side-on fish, with the start at the nose and the tail on the far end, so the run flows one way and the fish's outline alone says what it is.",
  "say": "Right, let's do a fish, side on, nose on the left. I'm sketching it on the pad now, so we know the plan before anyone places a domino. Start's at the nose.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 7,
  "point": [4, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[4, 10], [8, 5], [15, 4], [22, 6], [26, 9]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[4, 10], [8, 15], [15, 16], [22, 14], [26, 11]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[26, 9], [29, 4]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[26, 11], [29, 16]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[26, 9], [27, 10], [26, 11]]},
    {"type": "label", "x": 8, "y": 8, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Plan: fish, side on, nose left at START (4,10), tail right. Stroke 1 = top body (START to tail end), stroke 2 = bottom body from START, strokes 3-4 = tail fin branches off the body's far end, stroke 5 = tail join, label eye. I hold the pad. Next: hand pad to whoever takes stroke 1 (or do it myself), then trace strokes in order. Make sure someone is on stroke 1 since it leaves START."
}
